Hypotheses:
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

nda-11 (No reverse engineering): Not mentioned anywhere. NotMentioned.

nda-16 (Return of confidential information): Segment 26 says shall return documents within one week of written request. This is about return upon request, not upon termination. Hmm — "upon the termination of Agreement" — the document says return within one week of written request. This could be considered entailment for return of confidential information. The evidence is segment 26. Label: Entailment, evidence [26].

nda-15 (No licensing): No explicit statement that agreement grants no rights. The document doesn't grant rights explicitly. NotMentioned typically. Actually "No licensing" is often NotMentioned unless stated. NotMentioned.

nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-2 (None-inclusion of non-technical information): Confidential Information defined as "any information or data relating to any clients... business or affairs disclosed whether in writing, orally or by any other means" — this includes non-technical info, contradicting "shall only include technical information." Contradiction, evidence [23].

nda-1 (Explicit identification): Not mentioned that CI must be expressly identified. Definition says "any information... disclosed whether in writing, orally or by any other means" — implies not explicitly identified. Could be Contradiction. Typically in these datasets, if CI includes orally conveyed info, explicit identification is contradicted. I'd say Contradiction with evidence [23] or NotMentioned. Let me verify with human feedback.

nda-19 (Survival of obligations): Segment 29: "this Agreement shall remain in force in perpetuity." This means obligations survive. Entailment, evidence [29].

nda-12 (Permissible development): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-20 (Permissible post-agreement possession): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-3 (Inclusion of verbally conveyed information): Segment 23: "disclosed whether in writing, orally or by any other means." Entailment, evidence [23].

nda-18 (No solicitation): Segment 27: "I will not attempt to contact the employees, customers, creditors, suppliers or landlords of any client." This is no-contact, akin to no solicitation. Entailment, evidence [27]. Also segment 39 about staff. Typically evidence [27].

nda-7 (Sharing with third-parties): Segment 25: "not disclose it to any third party without the prior written consent" — this permits sharing with consent. Could be Entailment (may share with third parties with consent). In these datasets, "may share some CI with some third-parties" — if disclosure allowed with consent, it's Entailment. Evidence [25] (also [34]). Let me verify.

nda-17 (Permissible copy): Segment 25: "make no copies thereof" — no permission to copy. Contradiction? The hypothesis says "may create a copy in some circumstances." Document says make no copies — no exception. So Contradiction, evidence [25]. Or NotMentioned. Hmm. "make no copies thereof not disclose it..." The text: "Treat it as confidential and make no copies thereof not disclose it to any third party without the prior written consent" — ambiguous punctuation. Could read "make no copies thereof, not disclose it..." Copies prohibited absolutely. So hypothesis "may create a copy in some circumstances" is Contradiction. Evidence [25]. Let me check with feedback.

nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-13 (Permissible acquirement of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-4 (Limited use): Segment 25: "use it solely for the purpose as agreed between parties." Entailment, evidence [25].
